title: Large personal Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS restoration discovery
summary: Personally screen 378 candidate URLs and add 20 projects, with eleven explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root assistant personally searched 28 routes, screened candidate URLs against the current catalogue and inspected 31 primary-source repositories. This focused pass adds 20 game/application/OS restoration records with 11 explicit duplicate, scope or implementation decisions. Native source recovery is separated from generated instruction execution; portfolios and manuals are not counted as completed software. All exactness, gameplay and regression-test results remain attributed upstream, not independently rerun. The ST collection covers Batman, ACOPY and FastCopy Pro at repository root; Anacreon is correctly source-derived rather than binary-decompiled. Unknown AI use is not inferred from agent instructions. Large or encoding-mismatched source files retain immutable links rather than altered proof text.

sources.reason: Annotated disc OS ROM with named RSX, BIOS, BDOS, CP/M boot and XMON routines; source represents CPU-visible decoded bytes, not the scrambled physical EPROM.

Native Java game rewrites the recovered Amiga rules and renderer using extracted indexed assets and module playback. The separate emu directory retains an earlier routine translation with a small Amiga device model.
Partial engine/data investigation includes level-header loading, planar graphics decoding, reverse-engineering notes and extraction scripts.
C11 engine recovers fixed-point driving physics, original file formats and perspective renderer from the DOS executable; reads original data without executing the original binary.
Annotated DOS COM loader reconstruction includes pointer/EXEC parameter structures and a binary comparison build script.
Independent HnmPlayer reconstructs palette, compressed frame and timing behavior of Dune floppy LOGO.EXE; root Spice86 project separately supports original-code tracing and generated overrides.
Investigates Inner Worlds 1.2 retail extender/file layout, resource tables and ELF details, with a C++ extraction prototype.
Recovered Watcom DOS/4GW game logic is organized into C flight, mission, enemy, UI and sound subsystems; original files read at runtime without CPU instruction emulation.
Reverse-engineers QuickBASIC 4.0/4.5 quick-library container and dispatcher, with annotated Microsoft runtime listing, native loader and working library examples.
Reconstructs ZZT 3.2 engine, editor, scripting runtime and data builder from the lost-source release.
Restores Super ZZT 2.0 engine and editor source, with a clean replacement of TheDraw screen decompressor.
NASM reconstructs the DOS MZ image and its data; separately maintained C port translates routines with explicit DOS-style registers/memory and hardware adapters.
Translates original Turbo Pascal game units into JavaScript, preserving runtime RNG/numeric/set semantics while replacing the text UI with React galaxy views.
Restores serial terminal, ANSI, file-transfer and ASPECT components with native assembly/C and retained overlay analysis, plus source-owned experimental terminal builds.
Reconstructs Brad P. Taylor falling-symbol puzzle game and original data layout; compares native recovered code against original execution in a separate Unicorn test harness.
Recovered Supaplex game logic drives a new 3D presentation; repository retains debugger assembly, IDA annotations and intermediate C++ refactoring.
Multi-subject repository reconstructs Batman The Movie variants and annotated ACOPY/FastCopy Pro disk applications, including native loaders, game modules and WD1772/DMA routines.
Recovers cheat dispatch tables, controls/input and supporting routines from Carmageddon using matched Watcom debug-symbol research.
Annotated Thai-language investigation maps TSR interrupts, keyboard/printer paths, three-band glyph rendering, KU/TIS codes and configuration structures.
Evidence-linked analysis covers MM1 symbols/map overlays and events, MM2 contrasts, and MM3 archive cipher, LZHUF and executable unpacking, with executable Python readers.
Verified GitHub fork of tracked sarnau/AtariST-Little-Computer-People. Same title and recovery identity; do not duplicate under fork owner.
Verified fork of tracked movAX13h/DrRiptideDissected; README retains upstream authors and release links.
Same Harrier Attack Reloaded CPC project already tracked at cp-soft.itch.io; source repository is an additional evidence route, not a new game.
Inspected source identifies Apparat PROM Blaster for Apple II and CPU 6502, not PC/MS-DOS software. Outside this explicitly platform-focused pass.

Generated instruction-level C runs on explicit 8086 registers, flags, segmented memory, interrupts and device model. Retain for game-specific emulation audit rather than promote as a clean native engine; recompiler itself resides outside repository.
Reproduced operating manual only, with no program source or software reconstruction; documented bench testing is absent.
Reusable matching/decompilation pipeline, not an identified game/application restoration in inspected README. Retain for separate tooling pass instead of padding this focused batch.

Source-architecture and patch notes reference external QBASIC source, but repository has no reconstructed application or independent implementation. Retain as supporting research, not a completed disassembly.
WildDOS/HoBeta and SJASMPlus source identify a Z80 Spectrum-family application, not PC/MS-DOS. Relevant retro work but outside this pass platform scope.

Browser remaster statically translates 8086 instructions into register/flag/segmented-memory execution with device modeling. Assembly recovery is present, but retain for explicit game-specific emulation audit rather than count as a native high-level rewrite.
Repository is AMOS 3D format sample data from Aminet, with no implemented parser or reconstructed application.

decisions.title: Vortex VDOS 2.11-X — CPC decoded ROM disassembly
decisions.reason: Annotated disc OS ROM with named RSX, BIOS, BDOS, CP/M boot and XMON routines; source represents CPU-visible decoded bytes, not the scrambled physical EPROM.

decisions.title: Nibby Nibble — native Java reconstruction
decisions.reason: Native Java game rewrites the recovered Amiga rules and renderer using extracted indexed assets and module playback. The separate emu directory retains an earlier routine translation with a small Amiga device model.

decisions.title: OpenVikings — partial Lost Vikings engine recovery
decisions.reason: Partial engine/data investigation includes level-header loading, planar graphics decoding, reverse-engineering notes and extraction scripts.

decisions.title: SkyRoads — portable recovered C engine
decisions.reason: C11 engine recovers fixed-point driving physics, original file formats and perspective renderer from the DOS executable; reads original data without executing the original binary.

decisions.title: DESQview DEVICE.COM — reassemblable driver loader
decisions.reason: Annotated DOS COM loader reconstruction includes pointer/EXEC parameter structures and a binary comparison build script.

decisions.title: Dune floppy LOGO — standalone HNM playback recovery
decisions.reason: Independent HnmPlayer reconstructs palette, compressed frame and timing behavior of Dune floppy LOGO.EXE; root Spice86 project separately supports original-code tracing and generated overrides.

decisions.title: Inner Worlds — early executable and resource investigation
decisions.reason: Investigates Inner Worlds 1.2 retail extender/file layout, resource tables and ELF details, with a C++ extraction prototype.

decisions.title: JetStrike DOS CD — SDL3 C reconstruction
decisions.reason: Recovered Watcom DOS/4GW game logic is organized into C flight, mission, enemy, UI and sound subsystems; original files read at runtime without CPU instruction emulation.

decisions.title: QuickBASIC QLB — library runtime reconstruction
decisions.reason: Reverse-engineers QuickBASIC 4.0/4.5 quick-library container and dispatcher, with annotated Microsoft runtime listing, native loader and working library examples.

decisions.title: The Reconstruction of ZZT — Turbo Pascal source
decisions.reason: Reconstructs ZZT 3.2 engine, editor, scripting runtime and data builder from the lost-source release.

decisions.title: The Reconstruction of Super ZZT — Pascal recovery
decisions.reason: Restores Super ZZT 2.0 engine and editor source, with a clean replacement of TheDraw screen decompressor.

decisions.title: Alley Cat — NASM reconstruction and qualified C port
decisions.reason: NASM reconstructs the DOS MZ image and its data; separately maintained C port translates routines with explicit DOS-style registers/memory and hardware adapters.

decisions.title: Anacreon — Pascal-to-JavaScript browser port
decisions.reason: Translates original Turbo Pascal game units into JavaScript, preserving runtime RNG/numeric/set semantics while replacing the text UI with React galaxy views.

decisions.title: ProComm Plus 2.01 — incremental DOS reconstruction
decisions.reason: Restores serial terminal, ANSI, file-transfer and ASPECT components with native assembly/C and retained overlay analysis, plus source-owned experimental terminal builds.

decisions.title: FallOut 1991 — reconstructed puzzle-game C
decisions.reason: Reconstructs Brad P. Taylor falling-symbol puzzle game and original data layout; compares native recovered code against original execution in a separate Unicorn test harness.

decisions.title: Superplex3D — recovered Supaplex logic prototype
decisions.reason: Recovered Supaplex game logic drives a new 3D presentation; repository retains debugger assembly, IDA annotations and intermediate C++ refactoring.

decisions.title: Atari ST disassemblies — Batman, ACOPY and FastCopy Pro
decisions.reason: Multi-subject repository reconstructs Batman The Movie variants and annotated ACOPY/FastCopy Pro disk applications, including native loaders, game modules and WD1772/DMA routines.

decisions.title: Carmageddon — early cheat/input reconstruction
